Qatar turns to US LNG to cushion Iran war losses
Published: November 2, 2026 | Author: Dalga Khatinoglu, Oil, gas and Iran economic analyst
(Extracted summary of article text)
Qatar is securing long-term US liquefied natural gas supplies to protect its revenues amid disruptions from the ongoing conflict. The country depends heavily on shipping through the Strait of Hormuz.
Iranian missile strikes in March damaged two liquefaction units at Ras Laffan, eliminating approximately 12.8 million tonnes of annual capacity—roughly 17% of Qatar's pre-war output. Qatar's LNG exports plummeted to just 4.58 million tonnes in the third quarter, down from over 19 million tonnes a year earlier.
QatarEnergy holds a 70% stake in the Golden Pass LNG project in Texas, with production beginning March 30, 2026. The company also signed agreements with Cheniere Energy for 4 million tonnes annually and with Woodside for up to 3 million tonnes annually, with deliveries beginning in 2030.
Iran lost approximately 130 million cubic metres daily of gas production capacity—around 16% of last year's total output.
Qatar continues mediating between Iran and the United States while managing maritime security challenges in the Persian Gulf.
